description: Table 2 is a rendered text table (no plots or micrographs) listing Rietveld-refinement output for a mechanically alloyed non-equiatomic high-entropy steel (Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1) milled for 25 h, 30 h and 35 h. The header prints the fit quality of each refinement: 25 h, GoF = 1.08, χ² = 1.18; 30 h, GoF = 1.14, χ² = 1.29; 35 h, GoF = 1.10, χ² = 1.22. Phase columns are BCC, γ-brass type and Si for 25 h and 30 h, with an additional B2-type column appearing only at 35 h. Rows are Lattice Parameter (nm), Volume (Å³), Weight fraction, Crystallite Size (nm), Microstrain (×10⁻⁴) and Dislocation density (m⁻²) (×10¹⁸). BCC keeps a = 0.286 nm at every milling time, γ-brass type a = 0.872 nm, Si a = 0.543 nm and B2-type a = 0.290 nm. BCC weight fraction falls 74.4 → 73.0 → 64.0 while γ-brass type rises 21.0 → 23.5 → 27.0. BCC crystallite size decreases 17 → 15 → 13 nm, γ-brass type 13 → 12 → 10 nm and Si 20 → 13 → 14 nm. Microstrain increases monotonically for every phase with milling. Dislocation density is tabulated only for BCC (1.94, 2.67, 3.97 ×10¹⁸ m⁻²); all other cells are dashes.

observations.observation: A B2-type phase column is present only for the 35 h milling condition, with lattice parameter a = 0.290 nm and weight fraction 6.0; the 25 h and 30 h columns list only BCC, γ-brass type and Si.
Lattice parameters are essentially unchanged with milling for BCC (a = 0.286 nm), γ-brass type (a = 0.872 nm) and Si (a = 0.543 nm) at all three milling times.
BCC weight fraction decreases from 74.4 (25 h) to 73.0 (30 h) to 64.0 (35 h), while γ-brass type weight fraction increases from 21.0 to 23.5 to 27.0 over the same times.
Crystallite size decreases with milling for BCC (17, 15, 13 nm), γ-brass type (13, 12, 10 nm) and Si (20, 13, 14 nm) at 25, 30 and 35 h respectively.
Microstrain (×10⁻⁴) increases for every phase with milling time, e.g. BCC 10,849 → 13,195 → 17,013 and γ-brass type 13,731 → 15,445 → 18,829.
Dislocation density is tabulated only for the BCC phase (1.94, 2.67 and 3.97 ×10¹⁸ m⁻² at 25, 30 and 35 h); the cells for γ-brass type, B2-type and Si contain dashes.
Unit-cell volumes are given only for the 35 h B2-type phase (24.39 Å³) in addition to BCC (23.39 Å³), γ-brass type (698.33 Å³) and Si (160.10 Å³).
The caption states that Table 2 shows the variation in phase fraction, lattice strain, crystallite size and dislocation density with milling of the non-equiatomic HES.
The citing text states the crystallite size and lattice strain were calculated by Rietveld refinement using GSAS-II.

The citing text states crystallite size was tuned in the range ~13–17 nm for the BCC phase and ~10–13 nm for the γ-brass type phase, and that Si crystallite size decreased from 20 nm to 14 nm as milling extended from 25 h to 35 h.
The citing text states the lattice strain increased for all phases as milling progressed, attributed to atomic size difference, mechanical deformation and an increased grain-boundary fraction.
The citing text states the dislocation density shows negligible change with milling time — a claim the table's BCC values (1.94 → 3.97 ×10¹⁸ m⁻², roughly doubling) do not obviously support.
The citing text notes only a slight change in the amount of phase fraction for the BCC and γ-brass type structures, whereas the table shows BCC dropping by about 10 weight-fraction units at 35 h.

subfigures.description: Single rendered table: columns grouped by milling time (25 h, 30 h, 35 h) with GoF and χ² printed under each time; phase sub-columns BCC, γ-brass type, Si for 25/30 h and BCC, γ-brass type, B2-type, Si for 35 h. Six data rows: Lattice Parameter (nm), Volume (Å³), Weight fraction, Crystallite Size (nm), Microstrain (×10⁻⁴), Dislocation density (m⁻²) (×10¹⁸).
